title: Orchestrate enterprise model onboarding with priority scheduler and safe rollback policy
creator: Priya Reddy
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines an orchestration pattern for enterprise model onboarding that balances speed-to-availability with safety controls required by large customers. The goal is a reproducible flow that: (1) prioritizes enterprise requests by SLA/tier and business impact, (2) automates eval gating and version pinning policies, (3) supports staged rollouts with automated rollback triggers, and (4) provides operator runbooks and observability for post-launch regressions.

Problem & context:
Customer requests for new models (open-source variants, fine-tuned checkpoints, or third-party vendor images) are increasing. Currently intake is manual, decisions are ad-hoc and lack consistent telemetry to drive rollouts. Enterprise customers require explicit version pinning, predictable deprecation windows, and the ability to opt into canary/isolated capacity. We need a single orchestration pattern for PMs and SEs to follow so onboarding scales and reduces regression risk in production.

Proposed approach (high-level):
- Priority scheduler: requests scored by an enterprise priority formula (customer tier, expected qps, sensitivity of data, SLA). Higher score => expedited path and dedicated rollout lanes. Scores are stored as metadata on catalog entries.
- Eval gate: every onboarding must pass a gated eval suite (golden prompts, token-cost regression, latency percentile targets, hallucination/regression thresholds). Evals run in CI via infra harness and results posted to the model catalog page.
- Version pinning & compatibility: default behavior for enterprise onboards is to create a pinned version (vX.y) with STABLE/DEPRECATED flags and an explicit deprecation TTL. Pinning prevents automatic rolling upgrades unless customer opts in.
- Staged rollout & rollback policy: when gating passes, rollout uses staged percentages (5% -> 25% -> 100%) across capacities (hosted/dedicated). Rollback triggers include >15% increase in error rates, >10% regression in quality metric (BLEU/accuracy/AUROC depending on task), 95th percentile latency breach, or manual incident. Canary windows and automatic rollback are implemented by runtime flags and SLO monitors.
- Operator tooling & runbooks: add a console page for staged rollouts with manual override, clear instructions for emergency rollback, and audit logs for approvals and pin changes.

Trade-offs considered:
- Speed vs safety: Expedited enterprise path reduces time-to-value but requires additional test infra and human review for high-risk customers. We'll mitigate by richer automated evals and a dedicated SE review for Tier-1 onboards.
- Complexity in catalog: Adding states (PINNED, CANARY, DEPRECATED) increases catalog surface area; will maintain a compact UI by collapsing metadata and surfacing only actionable controls for PMs/SEs.
- Automation coverage: Full automated rollback depends on high-quality telemetry and per-model quality metrics. Initial rollouts will require hybrid approach (automation + human checkpoint) for novel model families.

Success metrics:
- Median time from request -> canary reduced to <= 5 business days for prioritized enterprise requests.
- Fraction of enterprise onboards with automated eval pass >= 90%.
- Zero Sev1 incidents attributable to onboarding regressions during first 90 days for Tier-1 customers (target).

Acceptance criteria (must be met before marking done):
acceptance_criteria: Priority scheduler implemented and scoring documented in Confluence
Eval pipeline integrated into CI with golden prompt suite and pass/fail thresholds
Catalog supports explicit version pinning and deprecation TTL metadata
Staged rollout UI in Console with manual override and audit logging
Automated rollback triggers wired to SLO alarms and tested in a canary experiment
Runbook and operator checklist published and reviewed by SRE and Security
